title: Accrual reliability, earnings persistence and stock prices

models.model_label: Next-year ROA on current ROA and the extended accrual components (Table 5 Panel C, final multivariate row)

columns: final multivariate row: all extended accrual components jointly

models.sample_description: Nonfinancial Compustat–CRSP firm-years from 1962–2001 with sufficient financial-statement data; financial firms with SIC codes 6000–6999 are excluded. The paper reports 108,617 firm-years across the sample and 40 annual cross-sectional regressions, but not the observation count in an individual annual fit.
models.method_reported: OLS regressions for the extended accrual decomposition
models.method_details: OLS regressions are estimated as annual cross-sections; the reported coefficients and t-statistics use the Fama–MacBeth approach across 40 annual regressions.
models.equation_text: ROA_{t+1} = r_0 + r_1 ROA_t + r_2 DCOA_t + r_3(−DCOL_t) + r_4 DNCOA_t + r_5(−DNCOL_t) + r_6 DSTI_t + r_7 DLTI_t + r_8(−DFINL_t) + u_{t+1}

fixed_effects.details: The paper reports annual cross-sectional regressions; it does not report fixed-effect dummy families. Estimation separately by year does not establish year fixed effects.

standard_errors.details: The authors report Fama–MacBeth time-series mean coefficients and t-statistics from 40 annual cross-sectional regressions; no clustering is reported.

evidence.quote: Regression results are based on 40 annual regression using the Fama and Macbeth (1973) approach.
Full equation: ROA_(t+1)=rho0+rho1*ROA_t+rho2*DeltaCOA_t-rho3*DeltaCOL_t+rho4*DeltaNCOA_t-rho5*DeltaNCOL_t+rho6*DeltaSTI_t+rho7*DeltaLTI_t-rho8*DeltaFINL_t+u_(t+1).

estimation_procedure.description: Estimate an OLS cross-sectional regression separately for each year from 1962 through 2001; report the time-series means and Fama–MacBeth t-statistics across 40 annual regressions. The sample total of 108,617 firm-years is aggregate; exact annual regression Ns are not reported.

evidence.quote: Panel C: OLS regressions for the extended accrual decomposition
Regression results are based on 40 annual regression using the Fama and Macbeth (1973) approach.
The sample consists of 108,617 firm years from 1962 to 2001.

preprocessing.description: Each component of earnings is winsorized at numeric bounds +1 and −1 in regression analyses.

evidence.quote: The source states: in regression analyses, each component of earnings is winsorized at+1and-1 to eliminate extremeoutliers.

preprocessing.description: Exclude a firm-year if required Compustat items 1, 4, 5, 6, 12 or 181 are missing in the current or previous year, or item 178 is missing in the current year; set missing optional items 9, 32, 34, 130 or 193 to zero.

evidence.quote: Specifically, we require availability of Compustat data items 1, 4, 5, 6, 12 and 181 in both the current and previous year and data item 178 in the current year in order to keep a firm-year in the sample.
If data items 9, 32, 34, 130 or 193 are missing, we set them equal to zero rather than eliminating the observation.

review_notes: Retained the final joint extended-accrual comparison, not the earlier simple earnings autoregression, total-accrual benchmark, coarser initial decomposition, or component-by-component univariate screens. The final row jointly includes all eight extended accrual terms plus current ROA.

The signs of liability terms are retained as negative variables (−DCOL, −DNCOL, −DFINL), matching the paper’s Table 5C column labels and equation. No fitted-value dependencies are required; all retained measures are constructed directly from balance-sheet changes.

missing_fields.sample_size: The paper reports a total of 108,617 firm-years and 40 annual cross-sectional regressions, but no exact observation count for any individual annual fit.

sample_extraction.data_section_full_text:
Our empirical tests employ data from two sources. Financial statement data are
obtained from the Compustat annual database and stock return data are obtained
from the CRSP daily stock returns files. Our sample period covers all firm-years with
available data on Compustat and CRSP for the period 1962–2001. We exclude all
firm-year observations with SIC codes in the range 6000–6999 (financial companies)
because the demarcation between operating and financing activities is not clear in
these firms. We eliminate firm-year observations with insufficient data on Compustat
to compute the primary financial statement variables used in our tests. <sup>8</sup> These
criteria yield a final sample size with non-missing financial statement and returns
data of 108,617 firm-year observations.
